items.title: Can CCS stop the AI boom from blowing the carbon budget?
items.summary: Data centres could account for 7 per cent of global electricity demand. At the UN climate summit, COP31, SINTEF’s Mona Mølnvik argued that gas power with carbon capture is a possible solution – as long as we don’t lock ourselves into solutions that can’t be fixed afterwards.

items.title: AlloySelect relaunches at Offshore Energy 2026 with new CCS screening preview
items.summary: Originally developed by OGC Energy in 2018, AlloySelect is now being relaunched with enhanced corrosion assessment and materials selection capabilities, alongside a new CCS module designed specifically for CO2 transport and storage applications.

items.title: Physically Motivated Dual-Branch Network for Multi-Scale CO2 Concentration Forecasting in Coal-Fired Units
items.authors: Xiushan Xia, Hailun Chai, Zerui Li, Kunyu Zhang
items.summary: Coal-fired power units increasingly operate under deep peak regulation, so accurate real-time prediction of flue-gas CO2 concentration is needed for combustion optimization and for feedforward control of post-combustion carbon capture. Hardware Continuous Emission Monitoring Systems suffer from measurement delay, while existing data-driven models are limited by two properties of furnace signals that are seldom addressed jointly: strong non-stationarity with distribution shift between lookback and prediction windows, and the superposition of a load-driven macroscopic trend with combustion-induced local fluctuations. This paper couples data analysis with model design in an end-to-end…

items.title: Formation Characteristics of CO2 Hydrate Particles and Slurry Transport Capacity under the Combined Effects of Low-Concentration DIOX and Met
items.authors: Yang Liu, Qinglu Meng, Xiaofang Lv, Peilong Li, Ye Tian, Chuanshuo Wang et al.
items.summary: Abstract CO2 hydrate slurry technology holds considerable promise for carbon capture and storage; however, its large-scale application is critically hindered by overly rapid hydrate formation, severe particle agglomeration, and unfavorable slurry rheological properties. To synergistically optimize the formation and transport performance of CO2 hydrate slurries, this study proposes a low-concentration DIOX/methionine (Met) combined system. Microscopic observation, particle interaction force measurements, and flow-model calculations were used to systematically investigate the formation kinetics, the particle cohesive behavior, and the transportation feasibility of CO2 hydrate in the combined…
